skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through a four-phase workflow for investigating bugs, testing hypotheses, and fixing verified root causes.
skill.summary: Find root causes before making fixes, using a structured debugging process.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, natural-language uses of at, and benign process text. I confirmed one medium-risk issue: the skill includes diagnostic shell examples that can expose environment or keychain details if copied without redaction. Manual review of SKILL.zip found only a duplicate SKILL.md, so no separate binary payload was identified.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic examples print environment and keychain state.
remediation.suggestion: Revise SKILL.md lines 90-105 to mask values, avoid broad environment output, and warn users not to expose secrets in logs.
Remove the archive from the published skill, or document why it is needed and verify it during release.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute local path in CREATION-LOG.md line 7 with a generic source description.

content.user_title: Debug Failures with Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Random fixes waste time and can create new defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through disciplined root cause debugging.
actual_capabilities: Applies a four-phase process: investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation.
Requires reproduction, error review, recent change checks, and evidence gathering before fixes.
Guides comparison between broken behavior and similar working examples.
Promotes one hypothesis at a time with minimal tests.
Escalates repeated failed fixes into an architecture discussion.
Connects debugging work to failing tests and verification steps.
limitations: It provides process guidance, not automated bug detection.
It may ask users to run local diagnostics or add temporary logging.
It depends on accurate evidence from the codebase and runtime.
Referenced companion skills are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to stop timeout guessing and identify why a test produces inconsistent results.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Bugs
use_cases.description: Follow a root cause checklist before changing production code under time pressure.

use_cases.title: Review Complex Fixes
use_cases.description: Compare proposed changes against working patterns before approving a risky fix.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Debugging Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic-debugging on this failure. First, list the evidence we need before proposing any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the four phases to this failing test. Identify reproduction steps, recent changes, and the first hypothesis to test.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Multi-Component Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic-debugging for this cross-service failure. Map component boundaries and propose safe diagnostics without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: I have tried three fixes. Use systematic-debugging to reassess the architecture and decide what evidence is missing.

output_examples.input: A flaky payment test keeps returning pending instead of completed.
output: Identifies status propagation as the focus.
Requests evidence from payment processing, event delivery, and persistence.

output_examples.input: A production build fails after a signing step.
output_examples.output: The skill directs the assistant to locate the failing layer, verify configuration propagation, and avoid changing signing logic prematurely.

output_examples.input: A team proposes a quick auth middleware fix.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for token lifecycle evidence and comparison with the middleware reference before accepting the proposed fix.

best_practices: Start with reproducible evidence before changing code.
Test one hypothesis at a time and record the result.
Redact secrets when gathering logs or environment details.
anti_patterns: Adding quick fixes before explaining the root cause.
Changing several variables in one test run.
Printing sensitive environment values during diagnostics.

faq.question: Does this skill fix bugs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the investigation and verification process before a fix is selected.

faq.question: Can I use it during incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to reduce guessing under pressure, while still supporting targeted diagnostics.

faq.question: Does it require tests?
faq.answer: It strongly favors a failing test or minimal reproduction before implementation.

faq.question: Will it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It may suggest diagnostic commands, but the user or agent controls execution.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-code systems?
faq.answer: Yes. The phases apply to build, deployment, integration, and runtime failures.

faq.question: How does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Claude Code can use it as a checklist for evidence gathering, hypothesis testing, and fix verification.
